<user_query>
Whenever I open an album, there is a shuffle button beside the Play All button. The shuffle text is being printed vertically with one letter below another due to which the button looks very big. Could you remove the 'Shuffle' text from that button and just keep the symbol?
</user_query>
Let me find the album detail screen where the shuffle button is defined.

input.query: Where is the shuffle button defined in the album detail screen?

content.text: I can see the issue. The shuffle button has both an icon and a `Text("Shuffle")` label. I'll remove the text and the spacer before it.

Done. I've removed the "Shuffle" text and the spacer from the shuffle button, keeping only the shuffle icon. The button will now be compact and match the size you'd expect, without the text stacking vertically.

<timestamp>Tuesday, May 5, 2026, 1:50 AM (UTC+9)</timestamp>
<user_query>
This worked. Thanks. Another issue I have is, When I click on an Artist, A list of albums appear for that artist. The album art picture is too big compared to the Album name and details. Could you reduce the size of Album art when I click an artist?
</user_query>
Let me find the ArtistDetailScreen to see how album art is displayed there.

The `AlbumCard` component is designed as a grid card — it uses a 1:1 aspect ratio that fills its width. When placed as a full-width list item in the artist screen, the art becomes a huge square. The cleanest fix is to replace the full-width `AlbumCard` usage in the artist screen with a compact row layout that has a small fixed-size thumbnail.

The issue is that in `ArtistDetailScreen`, the `AlbumCard` is used with `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`, so it stretches to full width. The `AlbumCard` itself has a square `aspectRatio(1f)` for the art, which means a full-width card will have a huge square image.

The best approach is to change the layout in `ArtistDetailScreen` to use a row-based list item instead of the card layout. But that would require quite a bit of refactoring.

Alternatively, I could add a `thumbnailSize` parameter to `AlbumCard` or create a separate compact list row composable. 

The cleanest solution would be to create a dedicated `AlbumListItem` composable that displays a smaller thumbnail (around 56-64dp) on the left with album details on the right, rather than trying to adapt the grid-focused `AlbumCard` for list usage.
